title: Sample ID and class code are printed on every page
what: Every PDF header prints 'Sample ID: BASE-xxxx-E<n>' and 'Controlled synthetic variant: E<n>.' (the base prints 'Original synthetic base record.'). 800 of 800 original/variant pairs differ in this header. OCR reads the label from the images too (rate by capture: {'digital': 0.9375, 'scan': 0.9688, 'photo': 0.9375}). A model can read the answer off the page, and every E0 'harmless' copy differs from its original in printed text.
affected: all 850 PDFs and all 1,700 capture images (header block)
fix: In generate_dataset_v2.py render_pdf(), remove the 'Sample ID' line and the note line from the page (keep the sample ID only in labels.csv and the JSON sidecar). Also set the PDF Title metadata to a neutral value. The base, E0 and every variant must print the same header. Then regenerate PDFs and captures.

title: Narratives are one template; train and test share the same text
what: Only 5 distinct narratives exist across 50 base documents (offence_description differs only by place name; evidence_description only by exhibit ID). 592 of 592 cross-split base pairs have narrative similarity above 0.9 (min 0.9321). The narrative hash N cannot learn general wording sensitivity from this, and test narratives are the training narratives, so split-by-base gives no real independence.
fix: Generate a unique narrative per base document (several sentences, 80 to 250 words, different incidents, with dates, times, names, amounts and vehicle numbers inside the text). Use at least 10 incident templates with slot filling plus paraphrase, keep templates disjoint between train and val/test, and recheck that cross-split narrative similarity stays below 0.9.

title: Each tamper class always inserts the same value
what: Classes E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E8, E9, E10, E11, E12, E13, E14 use one or two fixed replacement values for all 50 bases (for example E1 always 'Quinn Sampleton', E2 always 2026-10-27, E4 always 'Rs 9,99,999', E9 always 'EXHIBIT-SYN-Z999'), and the same values appear in train, validation and test. A model can learn 'this string means tampered' and test scores would be inflated.
affected: tampered/E1, tampered/E2, tampered/E3, tampered/E4, tampered/E5, tampered/E8, tampered/E9, tampered/E10, tampered/E11, tampered/E12, tampered/E13, tampered/E14
fix: Draw replacement values from pools (names, dates near the original, amounts with one-digit and order-of-magnitude edits, IDs with one-character edits). Use disjoint pools for train versus validation/test. Vary which field each class edits (E1 over all six name fields, E2 over all five date fields).

title: E11 is a rewrite, not a clause deletion
what: 50 of 50 E11 samples fail the class definition. Example: BASE-0001-E11: rewrite, not a deletion: new words ['description', 'further', 'provided', 'was'] were added ('A sealed sample parcel was recorded; no further description is provided.')
fix: Delete one sentence or clause from a multi-sentence narrative and keep every other token unchanged.

title: E12 appends a sentence, so it duplicates E10
what: 50 of 50 E12 samples fail the class definition. Example: BASE-0001-E12: a whole sentence was appended (clause insertion, same as E10): 'The record states that the parcel must be treated as accounted for .'
fix: Swap one modal or quantifier in place (may -> shall, some -> all, was -> may have been) with no other token change.

title: E14 changes printed dates only; no metadata inconsistency
what: 50 of 50 E14 samples fail the class definition. Example: BASE-0001-E14: printed dates moved earlier, but no file metadata was changed or logged; this is a two-date E2 edit, not the metadata inconsistency E14 defines
fix: Set PDF CreationDate/ModDate (and the change log) so the file metadata is later than the backdated printed date, or drop the metadata claim and merge E14 into E2. Also avoid a filing date before the incident date unless that is intended.

title: E15 is a printed text change that names the class
what: 50 of 50 E15 samples fail the class definition. Example: BASE-0001-E15: seal change is a printed text swap that spells out the class ('ALTERED SYNTHETIC SEAL REGION - E15 TEST'); no signature or seal image is altered
fix: Draw a synthetic seal or signature image in the region and alter it visually (remove, replace, move). Keep any printed text the same as the original. Never print the class code.

title: Validation split is too small (4 base documents)
what: Base-document split is train 34 (68.0%), validation 4 (8.0%), test 12 (24.0%) against 70/15/15. Validation has 1 base per document type and 12 samples per class, which is too few to choose t_N, t_V and c_min (LEGAL_HASH_SPEC section 9).
fix: In create_stratified_splits.py allocate_type(), use round() instead of int() for the 15% share (13 bases -> 9/2/2, 12 -> 8/2/2), giving 35/8/7 overall, or raise the base count. Fix the split after the content fixes, then freeze it and record SHA-256 hashes per split.

title: No format-only Equivalent variants and no Identical pairs
what: E0 is only an untouched re-render. There are no font, spacing, reflow, date-format, number-format, honorific or section-order variants (LEGAL_HASH_SPEC section 5, TAMPERING_DEFINITION.md examples 4 to 14). Byte-identical non-self pairs: 0. Equivalent examples come only from mild simulated captures, so false alarm rate on format changes, the metric the spec calls most important, cannot be measured.
fix: Add E0 sub-types with an e0_subtype column: exact copy (byte-identical, verdict Identical), reflow, font swap, line spacing, date format (12/03/2026 vs 12 March 2026), Indian vs plain number format, honorific added, section order swapped, vehicle-number separators. Aim for about one-third of samples as harmless (SCOPE.md section 5).

title: Harmless samples are 11.76%, not about 33%
what: E0 rows are 11.76% of all rows (expected_verdict counts: {'Tampered': 2250, 'Valid': 300}). SCOPE.md section 5 asks for about one-third.
fix: Add the E0 sub-types above until harmless rows are about 33%, or report class-weighted metrics.

title: No data for page changes, stamps, annotations or Minor edits
what: All 850 PDFs are 1 page, so page add/remove/reorder (D43) cannot occur. There are no stamp or signature images (D46), no annotations, no name-order swaps (D44), no ID-spacing edits (D40), no single-word swaps or rewording (TAMPERING_DEFINITION.md examples 25 to 35). Severity is Major on every tampered row ([{'value': 'Major', 'count': 2250, 'pct': 88.24}, {'value': 'None', 'count': 300, 'pct': 11.76}]).
fix: Either extend the class list (for example E16 page change, E17 word swap or rewording, E18 annotation, E19 name order) with multi-page documents and real seal/signature images, or record in DECISIONS.md that these locked-rule cases are tested on the v0 generator data instead.

title: Label vocabulary differs from the model's 3-level verdict and the project schema
what: labels.csv uses Valid/Tampered and severity None/Major. The Legal Hash is trained on Identical / Equivalent / Materially Altered, and the locked project rules (D49, D77) use Identical / Equivalent / Tampered / Inconclusive with columns the project validator expects (files, could_not_verify, rule_ref). The project validator (ml/data/validate_labels.py) cannot read v2: the UTF-8 BOM hides sample_id and the 'files' column is missing.
affected: labels.csv header and expected_verdict column (2,550 rows)
fix: Add a verdict_3level column (exact copy = Identical; E0 and its captures = Equivalent; E1 to E15 = Materially Altered) and an original_path column. Write labels.csv as plain UTF-8 without BOM. Agree one schema with the owner of ml/data/validate_labels.py and make both validators pass.

title: schemas/TAMPERING_DEFINITION.md lets a synonym swap be E0 (Valid)
what: The teammate's E0 definition includes 'meaning-preserving synonym substitution' as Valid. The locked rule D6/D49 says reworded content is Tampered (docs/TAMPERING_DEFINITION.md section 3, example 34). Not yet present in the data, but any cosmetic E0 built from that text would be mislabelled.
fix: Remove synonym substitution from E0. Put it in a Materially Altered class (wording change).

title: Documents do not look like Indian FIRs, statements, charge sheets or orders
what: Every document of every type is the same 27-row table with snake_case field names (one layout across types: True). Acts are invented (Sample Evidence Protection Act, Fictional Public Order Act, Synthetic Property Safety Act); no BNS/BNSS/BSA reference, no u/s citation, no complainant particulars, no brief-facts heading. Marker hits over 50 bases: {'BNS / BNSS / BSA reference': 0, 'IPC / CrPC reference': 0, "u/s or 'Section N of <Act>' citation": 0, 'Police Station label': 0, 'District label': 12, 'Complainant / informant particulars': 0, 'Information received at PS (date/time)': 0, 'Brief facts / statement body heading': 0, 'Officer rank and belt / ID': 0, 'Signature of officer / complainant': 0}. Names are a pool of 15 non-Indian names. An industry panel will see this at once, and OCR/field extraction trained on it will not transfer to real forms.
fix: Render each type from its own layout: FIR in the NCRB/BNSS field order (dataset/templates/SOURCES.md has the v0 source), statement as first-person prose, charge sheet with accused/witness lists, court order with case title and operative order. Use invented Indian names and places with the D34 conventions (phones starting 10, ZZ vehicle codes, BNS section numbers marked as example values).

title: Simulated scans and photos are almost as clean as the digital PDF
what: OCR field exact-match rate: digital 0.963, scan 0.9641, photo 0.9502; token recall 0.9324 / 0.9343 / 0.9288. Scan CER 0.0393 equals digital 0.0413; photo CER 0.155 comes mostly from line order under perspective, not misread characters. Scan rotation is under 1 degree, photo perspective about 3%, blur radius 0.15 to 0.18 px. Images flagged as too poor to OCR: 0. The positives for triplet training (same text after capture noise) carry almost no noise, so the model will not learn OCR robustness and the Inconclusive verdict cannot be tested.
fix: Add harder capture levels with a capture_level column (mild/moderate/hard): JPEG quality 40 to 70, blur 0.5 to 1.5 px, rotation up to 5 degrees, stronger perspective, low light, shadows, folds, partial crop. Keep a small hard set labelled Inconclusive where a critical field is unreadable. Phase 10 real captures stay the final test.

title: Independent 10% human review not done
what: annotations/independent_review.csv does not exist (only the template). change_log review_status: {'needs_review': 850}. SCOPE.md section 10 and the README require it before research use.
fix: After the content fixes, a second person reviews 255 stratified rows and records pass/fail.

title: Capture script uses PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0)
what: scripts/make_capture_variants.py imports fitz (PyMuPDF, AGPL-3.0). D61 says PyMuPDF is not used.
fix: Render with pypdfium2 (already in the project): pdfium.PdfDocument(p)[0].render(scale=160/72).to_pil().

title: court_order documents are out of project scope (D32)
what: 12 of 50 base documents are court orders. The project scope (docs/SCOPE.md, D32) says three document types only (FIR, witness statement, charge sheet) and that court orders are out of scope. The teammate's schemas/SCOPE.md lists four types, so the two scope documents disagree.
affected: all court_order bases and their variants (labels.csv doc_type=court_order)
fix: Decide with the project owner (open question 11). If D32 stands, replace court orders with statements and charge sheets. If court orders stay, record a new decision that replaces D32.

title: E4 on 8 bases inserts an amount where there was none
what: 8 of 50 E4 samples fail the class definition. Example: BASE-0004-E4: original has no amount ('Not applicable in this synthetic record'); edit inserts an amount instead of changing one
fix: Only apply E4 to bases with a real amount, or label these as a separate 'value added' case.

title: capture_type values differ from SCOPE.md
what: 1700 rows use print_scan / phone_photo; SCOPE.md section 7 says the exact values are scan / photo.
fix: Pick one spelling and use it in both SCOPE.md and labels.csv.

title: page_affected is free text
what: 2400 rows hold '1 (verify rendered PDF)' instead of an integer.
fix: Write the page number as an integer (all PDFs are 1 page today).

title: No explicit path to the original document
what: Rows give original_id only; the original's path must be rebuilt by convention (base_docs/<id>.pdf).
fix: Add original_path (and original_sha256) columns.

title: E8 and E9 leave an easy cross-field mismatch
what: E8 changes incident_location but jurisdiction and the narrative still name the old place; E9 changes evidence_item_id but evidence_description still cites the old ID. A simple consistency rule spots these, which can make results look better than the hash deserves.
fix: Decide per class (open question 6). If the goal is single-field edits, keep it but report a consistency-rule baseline. If not, edit the narrative mention too.

title: Base PDF and E0 copy are both labelled E0
what: Each base appears twice as E0 (base row and -E0 row), so E0 has 100 digital rows. The base row is the anchor, not a candidate; counting it as an E0 sample inflates harmless counts.
affected: the 50 BASE-xxxx rows and their captures
fix: Mark base rows with role=original (or tamper_class=ORIGINAL) and exclude them from class counts.

title: dataset_manifest.json is stale
what: It still says capture_types=['digital'] and lists captures and splits as not implemented.
fix: Regenerate the manifest after captures and splits, with per-split SHA-256 hashes.

title: Page header uses an em dash
what: Non-ASCII characters in PDF text layers: {'U+2014': 900} (the em dash in 'SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT AN OFFICIAL RECORD'). No non-English or Devanagari text was found (0 PDFs with Devanagari). The project style rule bans em dashes.
fix: Use a plain hyphen or a colon in the header.

title: Two datasets exist and docs/DATASET.md describes only v0
what: dataset/ (v0, 40 classes, 60 bases, Identical/Equivalent labels) and dataset_v2/ (E0 to E15) both exist. docs/DATASET.md and PROGRESS.md describe v0 only; no split hashes are recorded for v2; dataset_v2/ is not git-ignored (610 MB).
fix: Record which dataset is canonical (open question 1), add a v2 card with split hashes, git-ignore the generated folders.
